title: Lossless project context loading and decision ownership
summary: Make project context complete and verifiable at planner load and enforce single-owner Accepted Decisions.
description: Plan-core project-context modeling and completeness evidence; Pi and MCP planner-load and project-read surfaces; any necessary plan-server support; read-attestation semantics; Accepted Decisions ownership guidance and semantic operations; synchronized skills, capability inventory, and cross-harness regressions.
goals: Deliver every canonical project-level context field, all Requirements, and all project Accepted Decisions during planner load without silently treating truncated content as complete.
Make Pi and MCP expose equivalent, truthful project-context read contracts with explicit completeness evidence and safe continuation only when payload limits require it.
Keep task-start context scoped to feature, phase, and task work while preserving freshness-aware handling for context changed after project load.
Route each new durable decision to exactly one authoritative project, feature, phase, or task Accepted Decisions owner.
nonGoals: Redesign the Web UI Project Context presentation unless a minimal compatibility change is required by the new API contract.
Remove historical or legacy persisted decision data automatically.
Eliminate payload safeguards or place unbounded content into human-facing recaps.
Move project-global context into task-start context.
dependencies: Existing semantic accepted_decision_create/update/delete operations and AcceptedDecision schema.
Existing planner-load preparation, Project Guidelines read state, Requirement freshness tracking, and task-start context gates.
Existing Pi plan_get, MCP planner-show/planner-load, and bounded context helpers.
risks: Large Requirements or Accepted Decisions collections can exceed practical model or transport limits; partial delivery must remain explicit and non-attesting.
Changing decision_record may affect callers relying on its dual-write behavior, so compatibility must fail clearly or migrate to scope-aware semantic operations.
Removing redundant project context from task start before planner-load attestation is durable could create a context gap.
Pi and MCP expose different result channels, so tests must prove what is actually agent-visible rather than only inspecting UI-only details.
openQuestions: Determine the safest compatibility treatment for decision_record: deprecate with a typed redirect, or replace it with an explicitly scoped target contract.

Determine whether exceptional oversized project context should be automatically drained by the adapter or exposed through mandatory continuation tokens while keeping planner load incomplete until all chunks are read.

acceptedDecisions.title: A project-context read satisfies REQUIREMENTS_READ_REQUIRED for every requirement
acceptedDecisions.decision: recordProjectContextRead stamps sessionInfo on every requirement in the plan, not just requirements linked to the current task/phase. This means a complete, attested project-context read satisfies phase-scoped REQUIREMENTS_READ_REQUIRED gates everywhere, on any subsequent task, without a separate per-task requirement read.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: recordProjectContextRead only succeeds after verifyProjectContextChunks proves the agent received the exact, complete, fingerprint-matched set of every requirement in the plan (title, description, macro tasks) — not a count or a truncated excerpt. The agent has therefore genuinely read every requirement's canonical content, exactly as recordContextRead's per-requirement stamps attest for a narrower, task-scoped read. Gating on "has this session seen this requirement" is satisfied identically by either path; the two calls differ only in scope (whole plan vs. one task's linked requirements), not in the strength of the evidence. Treating a lossless full read as weaker than a partial one would force agents that already did the complete read to redo a strictly smaller one, with no correctness benefit. recordContextRead itself stamps only the ids it was given because it is intentionally task-scoped and has no evidence about requirements outside that scope; recordProjectContextRead has evidence about all of them, so it stamps all of them.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Implemented in packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts, recordProjectContextRead: every requirement in requirements.requirements gets upsertSessionInfo(sessionId, createdAt) applied, then the changed set is persisted through saveRequirements (fix for defect 1, routes through the same stale-write-guard and sessionInfo-merge path as every other requirement write). If this default should differ per gate or per harness in the future, that must be a new explicit decision, not a silent code change.

completionCriteria: Planner load proves lossless delivery of all canonical project fields, all Requirements, and all project Accepted Decisions, or returns an explicit incomplete state that cannot attest a successful read.
Pi and MCP project-read surfaces no longer promise a full read when agent-visible content is incomplete.
Task start does not duplicate stable project-global context and still detects context made stale after load.
Decision guidance and semantic operations select one authoritative owner and no longer instruct automatic feature-plus-phase duplication.
Focused core, Pi, MCP, server, skill/capability, and compatibility regressions pass, followed by the canonical bounded final gate at phase close.

tasks.title: Define lossless project-context delivery and completeness semantics
tasks.description:
Define the canonical harness-agnostic project-context read contract in packages/plan-core/src/recap.ts, packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts, packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts, and focused plan-core tests. Current planner-load recap construction exposes the project name, goal, and Project Guidelines but does not provide one complete typed payload containing project.description, descriptionRef, scope, outOfScope, technologies, tools, contentLanguage, chatLanguage, every declarative Requirement, and every project-owned AcceptedDecision. Existing buildBoundedAcceptedDecisionContext imposes an 8,000-character aggregate limit, so a truncated result can be presented even though downstream descriptions imply complete context. Introduce a single canonical project-context representation with explicit delivery evidence such as complete/truncated status, delivered and total counts, stable ordering, and safe continuation metadata only when payload limits genuinely require chunking. A partial page or chunk must never count as a successful complete read or satisfy project-load attestation. Preserve exact Requirement IDs, linkage, descriptions, macro-task states, timestamps, AcceptedDecision IDs and acceptedAt values, Project Guidelines separation, legacy data parsing, and transport-safe bounded human recaps. Add regressions for empty, normal, oversized, continued, stale, and legacy project context; prove that all chunks reconstruct the exact canonical data without loss or duplication and that incomplete delivery cannot be attested.

---

tasks.title: Deliver complete project context through Pi and MCP planner load
tasks.description:
Apply the canonical project-context contract to packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts, packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts, any required packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts support, synchronized planner skill sources, and representative integration tests. Current Pi plan_get advertises a full-plan read but its agent-visible content only includes project name, entity counts, active-task evidence, and a bounded project Accepted Decisions block; project description, goal, Guidelines, scope, technologies/tools, languages, and Requirement bodies are absent. Pi planner load exposes some fields only through a later ambient system prompt, while MCP planner-load structured agentContext contains the planner skill and bounded cross-scope decisions but omits most project context. Make explicit planner load deliver the complete project-level context to the agent in both harnesses, including the short description and descriptionRef, goal, scope and out-of-scope, technologies and tools, language preferences, Project Guidelines, every Requirement with canonical details, and every project Accepted Decision. Ensure human recap and structured agent payloads are truthful and consistent, automatically complete any necessary internal chunks or return loaded/contextComplete false with mandatory continuation actions, and never claim a full read from counts, UI-only details, or a truncated first chunk. Correct plan_get and MCP project-read descriptions/results so their declared completeness matches agent-visible content. Once durable load attestation exists, keep task-start delivery scoped to feature, phase, and task context; retain a targeted stale-context refresh when project content changes after load. Preserve explicit planner lifecycle, Guidelines read gates, Requirement freshness behavior, structuredContent-only host compatibility, Web UI startup metadata, bounded human-facing output, and existing active-task evidence. Add Pi/MCP/server regressions proving full visible delivery, incomplete-state behavior, continuation completion, post-load staleness, and parity across result channels.

---

## Carried-over defects in T403's committed code (folded in 2026-09-15)

T403 delivered the contract in packages/plan-core/src/project-context.ts and PlanStore, and it is committed at a0ea1ba. Three defects were found during review and left unfixed. They sit directly under this task's wiring, so fix them here, before two adapters depend on the current behaviour.

1. `recordProjectContextRead` (packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts) writes project.json and requirements.json with `atomicWriteJson` directly, bypassing `saveProject` and `saveRequirements`. Its sibling `recordContextRead` goes through the save methods. The bypass silently skips: `touchTimestamp()`, so the planner mtime marker is not bumped after the write; the `workDeviations` strip that `saveProject` performs and whose comment says workDeviations must never reach shared project.json; `mergeSessionInfo` against the on-disk copy; and the `assertSnapshotNotOlder` stale-write guard on requirements. It also re-implements the guidelines `updatedAt` stamping by hand. Route the forward writes through `this.saveProject` / `this.saveRequirements` inside `runAsBatch`, which also removes most of the hand-rolled rollback block.

2. `loadProjectContextDelivery` and `projectContextReadStateForSession` take the plan-root **write** lock for pure reads. Every other multi-document read in the store, including `loadAll()` which reads project, requirements, phases and features together, takes no lock at all. The invariant comment in packages/plan-core/src/write-coordination.ts previously read "Reads never take this lock, so secondary processes remain available for inspection" and was reworded to permit this. These are the only reads in the codebase that can block behind a writer, and the contract was changed to fit the code. The module already computes a fingerprint: read both documents, recompute, retry on mismatch. That needs no lock and no contract change. Restore the original invariant wording.

3. `recordProjectContextRead` stamps **every** requirement as read for the session. The sibling `recordContextRead` stamps only the requirement ids it was given. This means a project-context read satisfies phase-scoped `REQUIREMENTS_READ_REQUIRED` gates everywhere. That may be intended — a lossless delivery does contain every requirement — but it is a governance change that was never written down. Decide it explicitly, implement what is decided, and record the decision as a phase-owned Accepted Decision rather than leaving it implicit in code.

Verification for the folded work: focused plan-core tests plus the existing project-context regressions; prove the timestamp is bumped, that workDeviations cannot reach shared state, and that the read path takes no write lock. The canonical full gate belongs at phase close, not here (AGENTS.md rule 17).

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped both halves of T404.

CORE FIXES (packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts, write-coordination.ts):
1. recordProjectContextRead now runs inside runAsBatch and routes its project.json/requirements.json writes through this.saveProject/this.saveRequirements instead of atomicWriteJson, so it gets touchTimestamp(), the workDeviations strip, projectGuidelines sessionInfo merge, and the stale-write guard for free. Removed the now-unneeded hand-rolled rollback (each write is already atomic and idempotent to retry).
2. loadProjectContextDelivery and projectContextReadStateForSession no longer take the plan-root write lock. Added private readCoherentProjectAndRequirements(): reads project+requirements, fingerprints the pair, re-reads and re-fingerprints, retries (bounded, 5 attempts) until two consecutive reads agree, else returns the last read. Restored write-coordination.ts's original invariant comment: "Reads never take this lock, so secondary processes remain available for inspection."
3. Governance decision: recordProjectContextRead keeps stamping every requirement (not just linked ones), because verifyProjectContextChunks only succeeds on an exact, complete, fingerprint-matched delivery of every requirement — the same evidentiary strength recordContextRead has for its narrower scope. WIRING: added packages/plan-core/src/project-context.ts::buildProjectContextLoadReply (pure {text, structured} builder, same shape as handoff-reply.ts) and ::projectContextStaleAdvisory (non-blocking task-start advisory string). IMPORTANT CORRECTION found via existing tests: the full context text must NOT be concatenated into the human-facing recap channel — both harnesses have a pre-existing, tested invariant ("Accepted Decision context must not leak into the human recap") that a naive first pass of mine violated for the whole project-context text too. Updated packages/plan-core/planner-skill.md (and ran pnpm plugins:sync + plugins:check, both clean) to describe the contract and the loaded/contextComplete truthfulness rule.

Checked plan_get (Pi) and planner-show (MCP): both already scope their descriptions accurately to what they return; left unchanged.

New regressions cover: full visible delivery in both harnesses, the incomplete/oversized state (maxChars forcing contextComplete:false + nextActions, not attested), post-load staleness (task-start advisory after project mutated), and parity across MCP/Pi result channels.

Did not build a multi-round-trip chunk-continuation tool; oversized delivery returns contextComplete:false with a retry-with-larger-maxChars nextAction, since both adapters already hold the full delivery in one loadProjectContextDelivery call in-process. Did not run pnpm verify:final (excluded by the task; belongs at phase close). plan-server/src/serve.ts needed no changes — confirmed via grep it has no project-context delivery surface.

tasks.title: Enforce single-owner Accepted Decision routing
tasks.description:
Correct Accepted Decisions ownership semantics across packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts and schema-facing helpers, packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts, packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts, any affected packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts routes, synchronized planner skill sources, capability inventories, and focused compatibility tests. Current Pi ambient guidance says to record every new decision or user-agreed modification in both the relevant feature and phase, and the decision_record tool implements that policy by appending duplicate AcceptedDecision records to both owners. This conflicts with the semantic accepted_decision_create/update/delete operations, which already support project, feature, phase, and task targets, and it mishandles project-wide decisions discovered during task development. Establish an explicit ownership rule: project-wide decisions belong only to project.acceptedDecisions; feature-wide decisions only to that feature; phase-specific decisions only to that phase; genuinely task-local durable decisions only to that task. Do not duplicate decisions across scopes by default. Replace the incorrect guidance and make decision_record compatibility safe by either returning a typed redirect to the scoped semantic operation or evolving it to require an explicit owner without silently dual-writing. New durable decisions must not be stored only in legacy free-form decisions arrays, descriptions, notes, status logs, or completion summaries; those surfaces may reference canonical decision IDs but are not decision authority. Preserve existing AcceptedDecision IDs, acceptedAt timestamps, rationale and implementationNotes, explicit delete confirmation, read-context visibility, legacy persisted data, and atomic no-op behavior on invalid targets. Add core, Pi, MCP, server, skill, and capability regressions for each ownership scope, project decisions created during task work, prevention of duplicate cross-scope writes, compatibility behavior for decision_record, and correct context delivery after an owner is completed or archived.

---
**Completion summary:**
Enforced single-owner Accepted Decision routing across plan-core, Pi, MCP, and the HTTP API.

OWNERSHIP RULE: A decision has exactly one owner (project/feature/phase/task) chosen by scope, never duplicated. Encoded once in new packages/plan-core/src/accepted-decision-guard.ts (ACCEPTED_DECISION_OWNERSHIP_RULE, ACCEPTED_DECISION_RAW_REPLACEMENT_DISABLED_MESSAGE, LEGACY_DECISIONS_ARRAY_READ_ONLY_MESSAGE, buildDecisionRecordRedirectReply), exported from plan-core/src/index.ts, and imported by pi-adapter, plan-mcp, and plan-server so the wording/behavior lives in one place (AGENTS.md rule 4). Documented in packages/plan-core/planner-skill.md under a new "Accepted Decision ownership" section; packages/pi-adapter's ambient "Operational rules" bullet now cites the same constant instead of its own "record in both feature and phase" text. Ran pnpm plugins:sync (regenerated plugins/_shared/planner-skill.md.in and plugins/claude-code/skills/planner/SKILL.md) then pnpm plugins:check (clean).

decision_record TREATMENT CHOSEN: typed redirect, not an explicit-owner rewrite. packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts's decision_record tool still validates featureId/phaseId (atomic no-op on an invalid target, unchanged), but performs zero writes — it never calls updateFeatures/updatePhase — and returns buildDecisionRecordRedirectReply's guidance (details.written=false, redirected=true, redirectTool="accepted_decision_create") telling the agent to call accepted_decision_create with the single correct targetType. Chosen over an explicit-owner parameter because accepted_decision_create already is that explicit-owner operation; adding a second tool with the same write semantics would duplicate logic AGENTS.md rule 4 says belongs once. The removed dual-write compensation logic (feature-write-then-rollback-on-phase-failure) is gone because there is no longer a write to compensate.

LEGACY decisions ARRAY: the free-form `decisions: string[]` field on Project, Phase, and Task (Feature has none) is now read-only going forward. project_update/feature_update-equivalents, phase_update, task_update (Pi), planner-project-discuss/planner-phase-update/planner-task-update (MCP), and PUT /project|/phases/:id|/tasks/:id (HTTP) all reject a genuine change to `decisions` with errorCode LEGACY_DECISIONS_ARRAY_READ_ONLY, reusing the one core message. Pi/MCP reject any presence of the field (matches the pre-existing acceptedDecisions-raw-replacement precedent in those adapters); the HTTP routes compare against the existing persisted value (matching their own pre-existing acceptedDecisions precedent) so a GET-then-PUT round trip that merely echoes an unchanged `decisions: []` is not incorrectly rejected. Also fixed packages/plan-core/src/handoff-context.ts: handoff_write's taskUpdates[].decisions and phaseUpdate.decisions previously appended straight into task.decisions/phase.decisions (a second, less obvious path into the same non-authoritative array, reachable from both adapters since it is core code). They now render into the completion-summary/phase-update section text as a labeled "Decisions mentioned (not decision authority; record any durable decision with accepted_decision_create on its actual owner)" list instead.

PRESERVED, UNCHANGED: AcceptedDecision ids/acceptedAt/rationale/implementationNotes; accepted_decision_delete's confirmed=true gate; read-context visibility (Accepted Decisions remain visible on a completed/archived owner — new regression proves this); atomic no-op on an invalid target (accepted_decision_create/update/delete already did this via resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget, untouched). LEGACY DUPLICATED DATA: decisions already written to two owners by the old decision_record dual-write are left exactly as persisted — no automatic migration or de-duplication was added; this is a stated non-goal of the phase. The project-level legacy `decisions` array's existing migrate-on-load path (previewLegacyProjectContextMigration/applyLegacyProjectContextMigration) is untouched and still works on whatever legacy content is already on disk.

VERIFICATION: `npx tsc -p packages/<pkg>/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean for plan-core, plan-mcp, pi-adapter, plan-server (all four, confirmed twice, including after the revert-and-restore below). `npm test` in plan-core: 370/370.
